analysis.title: GS Materials - Oct 30...BP beats, RIO updates OT, TECK delivers, EGO ask, GLEN on track, BOL niggle, VALE friction, CS beats....GOOG v Mining
key_insights: Alphabet's post-market move on 10/29 erased more market cap than BHP, RIO, AAL, GLEN and others combined. The desk argues miners should produce less and show the value of their output, citing Codelco's 'value over volume' stance.

RIO traded about 2% below BHP overnight after a block-cave incident: underground seismic event, evacuation, 3 workers injured, no deaths. RIO said tremors are part of block caving. Separately, Antamina reported a death, on top of 4 mines in Chile losing people in recent weeks (5 mines in 5 weeks). The desk expects a knock-on impact to supply.

TECK was the standout print. The desk says AAL trades bound to TECK. QB ran well in October with no scheduled maintenance and TMF is not a throughput issue. In 2024 QB did 22kt in each of Nov and Dec, its two highest months.

EGO (Eldorado) had the messiest print, a reset that traded in line with AEM. Skouries is called 'TECK 2.0'. The critical path to commercial production is the filtration press going to 4 pads (commercial) and 5 (nameplate). The end-Q4 guide looks conservative but is a necessary precaution given the prior management team's record. The desk says the numbers already have a buffer.

GLEN: the copper guide bar was low and was met. Copper guide is now 810-870kt at the low end, GS at 824kt vs cons 833kt. YTD production is 599kt vs 268kt in 4Q25. Kazzinc is +15% vs consensus. Energy guide tightened to top end. Stock is 540p, not 640p. Remains top pick as GS favours base metals over bulks.

VALE beat: EBITDA about $3.5bn vs consensus $3.3bn (GS moved from $4.0bn). Iron ore fines and copper production were lower, pellets and nickel better. Guidance reiterated, with copper and nickel in the upper half. Iron ore realised price $85.10 vs cons $86, down 10% q/q. C1 costs +12% q/q, all-in costs +21% y/y, capex at the lower end of the range.

BP: shares +1% at the start, beat on a beat-expected setup. Beats across divisions, concentrated in gas & low carbon and refining, which suggests exceptional trading. CFFO ex working capital $14.3bn. Plan to address GoM liabilities as the priority for excess cash rather than an immediate large cash return. Strategy day is Dec 15. Positioning is still 10/10 long.

BOL: record quarter and cheap stock, but operational issues remain at Odda and Ronskar, Aitik grade is an open question until the 2027 mine plan, and near-term cash conversion is still an ask. Working capital was up in Q3 and stays elevated in Q4. Garpenberg is on track for the 2027 guide.

Gold drifted lower after the FOMC despite a 'run it hot' comment from parts of the Fed. A December hike is priced, oil is near $115, and PCE was in line. The desk reads the market as saying 'call me in 2027'.

October was brutal for materials. The desk sees no comparable month in 11 years. Copper is $14k, gold $4k, iron ore $90, zinc $3,800. SXPP is +14.6% YTD, GS Miners basket +8%, Big Oils +61%, gold basket flat, silver -7%, PGMs -25%.

Prysmian is adding a Texas copper mill as part of a more than EUR700 million ($780 million) investment programme and sees no sign of a slowdown in data-center demand or critical delays or cancellations.

Capstone 3Q26 EBITDA was $358M (+1% q/q, +44% y/y), beating GSe and Visible Alpha consensus by 9% and 7%, on lower sulphide costs at Mantoverde. Pinto Valley was weak. FY26 copper production is at the low end of guidance (200kt vs GSe 208kt) and cash cost at the top end ($2.75/lb vs GSe $2.86/lb). Santo Domingo FID is the focus.

China A-shares had a sharp risk-off morning led by AI hardware. CPO and PCB stocks gapped down more than 10% at the open on Q3 misses and margin compression, then losses narrowed. Flows rotated to CRO and Baijiu. Robotics declined after Unitree's Q3 report showed R&D-driven profit pressure.

market_movers.rationale: Initiated Glencore's Australian CDI (GLC.AX) with a Buy. The target uses a 50:50 blend of 1x NAV and 6.5x EV/EBITDA. GLEN is the desk's top pick and 2026E EBITDA is cut 2%.
Boliden: 2026 EBITDA lowered about 1% for SepQ actuals. 2027-29 EBITDA up 1-2% on minor cost revisions. Focus on execution into 2027.
Neste: strong 3Q delivery, EBITDA revisions for 2026/27/28E of +6/+2/+5%, well positioned for tightening renewable diesel markets.
Repsol: strong delivery and refining environment. FY26 buyback of EUR1.8bn implies a 10% shareholder return yield. 2026/27 EPS cut by 0.5%/0.2%.
Technip Energies: margin recovery underway, EPS changes of -1.2%/+5.9%/-0.8% for 2026/27/28E, next award cycle in focus.
OMV: solid CFFO driven by refining, petchems margins weak. Adjusted EPS changes of +4.3%/+5.1%/-1.9% for 2026E/27E/28E.
Beat across divisions on exceptional trading. Positioning is 10/10 long and strategy day is Dec 15.
The desk says the market will not give credit until Skouries reaches commercial production. The filtration press is the last constraint and the numbers already carry a buffer.
The desk would bet on TECK in Q4. QB is running well with no scheduled maintenance.

risk_factors: Mine safety incidents: RIO block-cave seismic event, an Antamina death, and 4 Chile mines losing people. These could reduce supply.
Weak sentiment in materials after a bad October: lithium, aluminium and iron ore are weak.
Hawkish Fed: a December hike is priced and oil is near $115, which pressures gold.
AI-related headline risk can overwhelm miners' market caps, as the GOOG move did.
EGO execution risk at Skouries, from the filtration press and the prior management's record.
BOL operational issues at Odda, Ronskar and Aitik grade, and near-term cash conversion.
China A-share risk-off in AI hardware and weak consumer sentiment.
vol_and_positioning: BP positioning is still 10/10 long, described as a massive consensus long.
Overnight RIO traded about 2% below BHP after the block-cave incident.
geopolitical: The desk mentions Chinese A-shares risk-off on AI hardware earnings and the 2018 US-China trade war 1.0 as the closest historical comparison for October's market conditions.

tension_points.bull_case: The desk says GLEN's copper guide bar was low and was met, YTD production of 599kt is far above last year's pace, and QB and Collahuasi look set for a strong quarter.
tension_points.bear_case: Some commentators were negative on the copper guide and the desk expects numbers to come down 5-10kt. Capstone's FY26 copper is at the low end of guidance.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Glencore Q4 copper production falling short of the low end of the 810-870kt guide.

tension_points.bull_case: The end-Q4 guide looks conservative, the numbers carry a buffer and success would mean a big win.
tension_points.bear_case: The market will not give credit until commercial production, the filtration press is the only constraint, and prior management had a poor track record.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Skouries failing to bring the filtration press to 4 pads by end Q4.
